_about: Tax-year rates and limits the engine reads. Every leaf is {value, source, tax_year}; engine code reads values only through engine/config.py, so nothing is hard-coded in a calculator. DRAFT: hand-written by the engine until the Documents and retrieval config lands; engine/config.py is the only file to change if the final format differs. 2026 tables are used for the January 2027 cohort until the 2027 Pub 15-T and DR 1098 publish.

line_1g.note: Worksheet 1A line 1g when the Form W-4 Step 2 box is NOT checked; 0 when it is.

schedules.note: Annual Percentage Method rows [at_least, but_less_than (null = no cap), base_tax, rate]. Tentative annual withholding = base_tax + rate * (adjusted annual wage - at_least).
schedules.source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p15t.pdf (2026) Percentage Method Tables for Automated Payroll Systems, p. 12. Married filing separately uses the Single rows.

additional_rate.source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p15.pdf (2026) section 9, Additional Medicare Tax withholding

additional_threshold.note: Employer withholds the additional rate on wages over this amount in the calendar year, regardless of filing status.

allowance.note: DR 1098 line 2a when the employee did not submit a DR 0004.

employee_rate.note: 0.88% premium, up to half from the employee. Drops to 0.86% (0.43%) in 2027.

wage_base.note: FAMLI premiums stop at the Social Security wage base.

local.note: Colorado occupational privilege taxes, employee share. Keys are city names as the quiz writes them; each city carries its own source (the engine reads only employee_monthly and min_monthly_wages, and charges the tax when monthly wages are at least min_monthly_wages). Aurora is not here: its tax was repealed effective Jan. 1, 2025 (https://www.auroragov.org/business_services/taxes/occupational_privilege_tax), so a worker there owes no city tax.

Glendale.note: The city says more than $750 a month; the engine's at-least differs only at exactly $750.

Sheridan.note: The city code sets the $3; the $500 threshold is from Metro Denver's table, not the city. Confirm with the city's tax office.

total_additions_limit_415c.note: Employee deferrals plus all employer money (match, non-match, credits swept in) per year; catch-up contributions don't count.

roth_ira_phaseout.note: [start, end] of modified AGI over which the Roth IRA limit phases to zero.

roth_ira_phaseout_round_up_to.note: A reduced limit is rounded up to the next multiple of this.
roth_ira_phaseout_round_up_to.source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p590a.pdf, Figuring Your Reduced Roth IRA Contribution Limit

roth_ira_phaseout_minimum.note: A reduced limit above zero but below this is raised to this.
roth_ira_phaseout_minimum.source: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p590a.pdf, Figuring Your Reduced Roth IRA Contribution Limit

section_423_annual_limit.note: Stock valued at the offering-start price, per calendar year.

emergency_fund_target_months.note: Rule of thumb, not a tax rule: months of expenses saved before the ESPP, Roth IRA or extra 401(k).
emergency_fund_target_months.source: FirstPaycheck proposal, contribution order (Appendix A examples 3-5)

max_employer_stock_percent.note: Rule of thumb, not a tax rule: keep employer stock to about this share of investments.
max_employer_stock_percent.source: FirstPaycheck proposal, Appendix A example 4 sell-or-hold rule of thumb; eval/cases/ex4-espp.json
